dedupe_keys.name: fcc 25 8 notice of proposed rulemaking and order on the 900 mhz band 896 901 935 940 mhz for private broadband used by utilities and critical infrastructure january 2025

description: This FCC document proposes rules to open the whole ten megahertz of the 900 MHz band, 896-901 and 935-940 MHz, to private broadband, in a framework that lets broadband proponents and incumbent licensees agree county by county to transition the band. It records the band's regulatory history from the 2017 inquiry, the 2018 application freeze and the 2019 and 2020 realignment decisions, a petition by utilities and their alliance, and the current allocation, and states that hundreds of entities hold licences in the band, including utilities, railroads, and trucking, manufacturing and oil and gas firms. The Commission says the aim is to meet the growing private wireless capacity needs of utilities, railroads and other critical infrastructure. Access: free 58-page PDF from the FCC document system; no licence is stated. Coverage is the United States, with county-level processes for licensing. Caveats: it is a proposed rulemaking, so the rules were not final at adoption, and it describes spectrum policy, not coverage maps. It suits capacity planning and resilience studies of utility communications for grid and pipeline operations, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
